article.title: ETH Zurich 3D Simulations Suggest Venus Is Still Tectonically Active as Rift Flanks Widen 3 to 10 Centimeters a Year
article.summary: New ETH Zurich simulations find Venus's rift flanks widening 3 to 10 centimeters a year, suggesting the planet is still tectonically active.
article.body_markdown:
## Overview

New three-dimensional computer simulations built by researchers at ETH Zurich suggest that Venus's rift valleys are geologically young and still actively widening, challenging the long-held assumption that the planet's rift systems are ancient, dormant scars, according to [ETH Zurich](https://ethz.ch/en/news-and-events/eth-news/news/2026/07/venus-dead-far-from-it.html). The findings, published in the journal Nature Geoscience, show that Venus's rift flanks — broad ridges that form along the edges of rift valleys — widen at rates of 3 to 10 centimeters per year, according to [ETH Zurich](https://ethz.ch/en/news-and-events/eth-news/news/2026/07/venus-dead-far-from-it.html) and [Phys.org](https://phys.org/news/2026-07-young-rift-flanks-venus-tectonically.html).

## What We Know

- Venus's rift valleys can span up to 10,000 kilometers, comparable in scale to Earth's African Rift Valley, according to [ETH Zurich](https://ethz.ch/en/news-and-events/eth-news/news/2026/07/venus-dead-far-from-it.html) and [Phys.org](https://phys.org/news/2026-07-young-rift-flanks-venus-tectonically.html).
- Planetary scientists have generally held that Venus's rift valleys "originated more than 100 million years ago" and were "remnants of the past," according to [Phys.org](https://phys.org/news/2026-07-young-rift-flanks-venus-tectonically.html). The new simulations instead show that rift flanks form "when the rifts are geologically young," implying that at least some of Venus's rift systems are far younger than that long-standing estimate, according to [ETH Zurich](https://ethz.ch/en/news-and-events/eth-news/news/2026/07/venus-dead-far-from-it.html) and [Phys.org](https://phys.org/news/2026-07-young-rift-flanks-venus-tectonically.html).
- The research was led by Xi Yang, a master's student, working under the supervision of Taras Gerya, professor of geodynamics in ETH Zurich's Department of Earth and Planetary Sciences, according to [ETH Zurich](https://ethz.ch/en/news-and-events/eth-news/news/2026/07/venus-dead-far-from-it.html). The study, titled "Recent active rifting on Venus revealed by wide rift flank uplifts," lists Yang, Gerya, and co-author A. Gülcher as authors, according to [ETH Zurich](https://ethz.ch/en/news-and-events/eth-news/news/2026/07/venus-dead-far-from-it.html).
- "The results help us to better assess the tectonic activity on Venus," Gerya said, according to [ETH Zurich](https://ethz.ch/en/news-and-events/eth-news/news/2026/07/venus-dead-far-from-it.html) and [Phys.org](https://phys.org/news/2026-07-young-rift-flanks-venus-tectonically.html).
- The team's method marks an advance over earlier research: previous models of Venusian rifting "had relied on simplified material assumptions and were mostly two-dimensional," while Yang's team simulated high-resolution, three-dimensional rifts for the first time, according to [ETH Zurich](https://ethz.ch/en/news-and-events/eth-news/news/2026/07/venus-dead-far-from-it.html).
- The simulated rift flanks are not purely theoretical: features predicted by the model "can also be seen in images of the Venusian surface from the Magellan probe during its 1990's mission," according to [ETH Zurich](https://ethz.ch/en/news-and-events/eth-news/news/2026/07/venus-dead-far-from-it.html) and [Phys.org](https://phys.org/news/2026-07-young-rift-flanks-venus-tectonically.html).
- One simulation compared a modeled crustal structure after 700,000 years of rifting against the real Dali Chasma rift system on Venus, according to [ETH Zurich](https://ethz.ch/en/news-and-events/eth-news/news/2026/07/venus-dead-far-from-it.html).
- Unlike on Earth, where "erosion gradually wears down features," Venus's rift flanks flatten over time through crustal relaxation rather than weathering, according to [ETH Zurich](https://ethz.ch/en/news-and-events/eth-news/news/2026/07/venus-dead-far-from-it.html) and [Phys.org](https://phys.org/news/2026-07-young-rift-flanks-venus-tectonically.html).
- ETH geophysics professors Paul Tackley and Gerya are among the researchers participating in the European Space Agency's EnVision mission, which is scheduled to launch in the early 2030s to study Venus, according to [ETH Zurich](https://ethz.ch/en/news-and-events/eth-news/news/2026/07/venus-dead-far-from-it.html) and [Phys.org](https://phys.org/news/2026-07-young-rift-flanks-venus-tectonically.html).
- The researchers say the modeling approach could also help improve the detection of rocky exoplanets, according to [ETH Zurich](https://ethz.ch/en/news-and-events/eth-news/news/2026/07/venus-dead-far-from-it.html) and [Phys.org](https://phys.org/news/2026-07-young-rift-flanks-venus-tectonically.html).

## What We Don't Know

- The study does not date individual rift valleys; it demonstrates a widening mechanism and rate rather than assigning specific ages to particular rift systems.
- Direct confirmation from orbit is still years away — the EnVision mission that could gather more detailed surface data is not expected to launch until the early 2030s, according to [ETH Zurich](https://ethz.ch/en/news-and-events/eth-news/news/2026/07/venus-dead-far-from-it.html).
